How it regulates stress: C3H15 is a negative regulator of thermotolerance. Heat stress suppresses C3H15 transcription and promotes its degradation, relieving C3H15-mediated repression of HSFA2. Increased HSFA2 then promotes HSC70.3 expression and heat tolerance.
Key Target(s) / Pathway: HSFA2; HSC70.3; heat-shock response
Evidence Type: Promoter-binding assays + genetic analysis + heat-induced protein degradation studies + expression analysis
Research paper: Integration of C3H15-mediated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation confers plant thermotolerance in Arabidopsis

How it regulates stress: C3H14 positively regulates basal defense against Botrytis cinerea mainly through WRKY33. It activates the WRKY33-ORA59 and WRKY33-PAD3 cascades, supporting JA/ethylene signalling and camalexin biosynthesis.
Key Target(s) / Pathway: WRKY33; ORA59; PAD3; JA/ethylene signalling; camalexin
Evidence Type: Mutant/complementation analysis + overexpression + gene-expression analysis + genetic epistasis
Research paper: The Arabidopsis CCCH protein C3H14 contributes to basal defense against Botrytis cinerea mainly through the WRKY33-dependent pathway
